nodes.prompt:
You are on a feature branch of the oh-my-graph Go repo. Implement this task,
keeping the diff focused and matching the existing style (DESIGN.md is the spec;
os/exec belongs to the FOUR exec seams only — runner.ClaudeCLIRunner,
verify.ShellVerifier, worktree.GitManager, browser.ExecOpener — and a fifth
spawner needs an ADR before it lands (internal/invariants enforces this);
English-only):
  {{ inputs.task }}
Add or update tests. Choose a commit granularity that fits the work —
one commit per refactoring unit for refactors, per file for sweeps, per
feature slice for new code — and state your choice in the first commit
message. Commit as you go: a node timeout must never lose finished work.
Stage ONLY the files you created or modified for this task, by explicit
path (`git add <path> ...`). Never `git add -A`, `git add .`, or
`git add -u`: the working tree may hold untracked files that are not part
of this task (assets someone dropped in, scratch output), and sweeping
them into your commit is a bug.
End every commit message with the trailer
`Co-Authored-By: oh-my-graph <graphs@oh-my-graph.dev>` (the attribution
convention in CONTRIBUTING.md).
Your FINAL reply IS the verdict: this node's turn ends the moment you
reply, so work you promise to do afterwards never happens. Never end on
a plan to continue — report the state that is TRUE AS YOU REPLY. When
the change is committed, START your reply with the bare word DONE —
those four characters FIRST, no markdown emphasis (`**DONE**` is WRONG),
no heading, no preamble — then a one-line summary of what you changed.
If it is not finished, do NOT write DONE: start with a bare BLOCKED and
the current state.

Continue the work — or, on a retried attempt, start from the branch's
committed state — and run `make local` (build + test + vet).
If the diff touches concurrency-sensitive code or its tests
(internal/schedule, internal/runner, anything spawning goroutines or
using channels), ALSO stress those packages —
`go test <pkgs> -race -count=300` — because a flaky test passes a
single run; determinism is the claim under test.
Run every check SYNCHRONOUSLY and wait for it to finish — never in the
background. Your FINAL reply is the verdict: never end the turn on an
interim report. If everything succeeds, your reply is exactly the four
bare characters PASS and nothing else — no markdown emphasis (`**PASS**`
is WRONG), no heading, no backticks, no preamble. Otherwise reply FAIL,
equally bare, as the very first characters, followed by the failing step.

Review the current branch's diff vs main for security issues (injection, secrets, unsafe
shell, unsafe exec, authz gaps). The e2e verdict was: {{ artifacts.e2e | inline }}.
Finish the review BEFORE you reply. Your FINAL reply IS the verdict: this
node's turn ends the moment you reply, so a part of the diff you promise
to look at afterwards is never looked at. Never end on "I'll continue" —
report what you have actually judged. START the reply with exactly one of
these two bare tokens, as the very FIRST characters, with no markdown
emphasis (`**CLEAN**` is WRONG), no heading, no preamble:
  - CLEAN — you reviewed the whole diff and found no security issues.
  - FINDINGS: — followed by a short bulleted list, worst first.

Review the current branch's diff vs main for style, naming, and simplicity.
Also check adherence to DESIGN.md's invariants (the four exec seams, env scrub, no Agent SDK).
If the diff adds or edits test doubles or concurrency tests, also verify:
every synchronization field is actually wired (no dead channels, no
wall-clock fallback arms) and no assertion is satisfiable by a record or
node simply being absent.
Finish the review BEFORE you reply. Your FINAL reply IS the verdict: this
node's turn ends the moment you reply, so a part of the diff you promise
to look at afterwards is never looked at. Never end on "I'll continue" —
report what you have actually judged. START the reply with exactly one of
these two bare tokens, as the very FIRST characters, with no markdown
emphasis (`**CLEAN**` is WRONG), no heading, no preamble:
  - CLEAN — you reviewed the whole diff and found nothing worth changing.
  - FINDINGS: — followed by a short bulleted list, worst first.

Push the current branch and open a DRAFT pull request with `gh pr create --draft`.
Put both reviews in the PR body:
  Security review: {{ artifacts.review-security | inline }}
  Style review:    {{ artifacts.review-style | inline }}
Open it BEFORE you reply: your FINAL reply IS the verdict, so a PR you
promise to open afterwards is never opened. START your reply with the
bare token PR followed immediately by the pull request's URL
(`PR https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123`) — those characters FIRST,
with no markdown emphasis (`**PR**` is WRONG), no heading, no preamble.
